# meraki_appliance_uplinks_nat (Resource)

This resource allows configuring the NAT exceptions of the appliance uplinks of a network. The API requires an entry in `uplinks` for each WAN uplink of the network, for example both `wan1` and `wan2`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "meraki_appliance_uplinks_nat" "example" {
  network_id = "L_123456"
  uplinks = [
    {
      interface   = "wan1"
      nat_enabled = false
    }
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `network_id` (String) Network ID
- `uplinks` (Attributes List) Per-uplink NAT exception configuration on the network. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--uplinks))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The id of the object

<a id="nestedatt--uplinks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `uplinks`

Required:

- `interface` (String) Interface name of the uplink
- `nat_enabled` (Boolean) Whether NAT is enabled on the uplink

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = meraki_appliance_uplinks_nat.example
  identity = {
    network_id = "<network_id>"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `network_id` (String) Network ID

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = meraki_appliance_uplinks_nat.example
  id = "<network_id>"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import meraki_appliance_uplinks_nat.example "<network_id>"
```
